title: Feedback synthesis — quickscans + decision log (Dec 2026)
body:
Purpose:
Quick-turn synthesis of December customer feedback scans (support tickets, CS interviews, two exec calls, and product surveys). This doc is deliberately short — capture signals, suggest action lanes, and record decisions to enable rapid engineering handoff.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Recurring, high-signal asks across customers (mid-market and platform customers primarily): 1) more transparent cost breakdowns per-route/model (token + infra cost), 2) stronger private/VPC onboarding docs + reference configs, 3) simpler canary/fallback controls in Console for mixed-model rollouts.
- Short-term experiments recommended (2–6 weeks): enhanced cost explainer + per-request sample calc; onboarding checklist + reference Terraform for major cloud vendors; Console toggle for "soft-fallback" with simulated failover trace.
- Medium-term (Q1 roadmap asks): model-variant families in catalog (auto-fallback choices), a dedicated "billing trace" in Console linked to token-level traces, and an eval-based regression alert for rollouts.

Raw signals (source annotations):
- Support tickets (35 sampled): many tickets labeled "unexpected billing spike" are actually engineering teams hitting different batching behaviors during scale tests. Common confusion points: tokenization differences across model variants and lack of per-call estimate.
- CS interviews (10 customers): Platform teams want an opinionated "cost SLO" suggestion for batching/kv-cache settings tied to target p99 latency. They want something they can copy-paste into infra docs.
- Product survey (n=78): Top three ranked asks: 1) clearer private deployment checklist (65%), 2) per-route history of model fallbacks (42%), 3) easier way to run local evals against production prompts (37%).
- Two executive customer calls: enterprise customers flagged auditability (tamper-evident logs + KMS integration) as gating for on-prem adoption.

Representative quotes (verbatim-ish):
- "We love Redwood runtime but can't explain to finance why token cost jumped during our load test." — infra lead, fintech startup
- "Our security team needs a turnkey VPC playbook; writing our own still takes weeks." — platform eng manager, healthcare ISV
- "When a model degrades, we want to see what fallback happened and why — currently it's a black box." — ML infra lead, adtech

Thematic clusters (short):
1) Cost transparency and debuggability (tickets, survey + interviews)
2) Private deployment onboarding friction (surveys + exec calls)
3) Rollouts + fallback observability (interviews + tickets)
4) Small UX asks (API ergonomics, clearer error codes)

Prioritization + reasoning (proposed buckets):
- P0 (weeks): Per-request cost estimator + simple billing explanation modal in Console; Onboard checklist + 1-click reference Terraform snippets (GCP/AWS/Azure)
  - Reason: High frequency, high customer frustration, low engineering scope to prototype (UX + small backend traces)
- P1 (quarter): Console: model-fallback history per-route + rollout trace; soft-fallback toggle (simulate before enabling); token-level trace export for billing reconciliation
  - Reason: Larger engineering but core to reliability story for enterprise deals
- P2 (post-Q1): Eval-linked regression alerts for rollouts; model-variant families and auto-fallback rules in catalog; improved error codes and SDK helper wrappers
  - Reason: Strategic, requires coordination with serving/runtime engineering and product

Suggested quick experiments (concrete):
- Experiment A: "Estimate this call" button on API docs and Console request inspector. Shows token estimate, model unit cost (USD), and an example worst-case bill for typical batch sizes. Metrics to watch: support tickets mentioning "billing confusion" over next 30 days; click-through rate on modal. (Owner: Product Dev + Docs)
- Experiment B: Private deploy "starter pack" repo: sample Terraform + VPC peering diagram + template systemd service for on-prem installer. Aim: reduce customer-reported setup time from weeks -> days in pilot group. (Owner: Solutions Eng + Private Deploys)
- Experiment C: "Rollback trace" feature (UX prototype): when a route switches model at runtime, record event + reason + p99 latency delta; surfacing this on Route Activity. Start as an event log for three pilot customers. (Owner: Console + Serving Runtime)

Tradeoffs and risks documented:
- Cost estimator accuracy: early estimator will be approximate; must include clear "how to interpret" language to avoid false assurance.
- Exposing fallback reasons may reveal internal heuristics; coordinate with legal/comms to frame messaging.
- Quick Terraform pack risks: may encourage unsupported topologies — include disclaimers and support matrix.

Decision log (short):
- 2026-12-06: Approve prototyping Experiment A + B (CS, Product, Solutions Eng).
- 2026-12-08: Console team to build minimal Rollback trace event (pilot for 3 customers) — agreed scope: event entries + link to request id; no live UI beyond an events tab.
- 2026-12-09: Docs to draft cost explainer content and sample calculations for public API docs.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: Coordinate pilot customer list and outreach for Experiment C (ETA 2026-12-16).
- Marcus: Create Terraform starter pack repo skeleton and initial GCP example (ETA 2026-12-13). Repo link to be added to Confluence page.
- Sophie: Draft cost explainer and API modal copy; tie trust language to billing export features (ETA 2026-12-10).
- Engineering (Console): Prototype Rollback trace event producer (ETA 2026-12-20).
- Solutions Eng (Ravi): Schedule 2 pilot private-deploy onboarding sessions and capture friction points (ETA 2026-12-17).

Open questions / things to research:
- How feasible is token-level cost attribution for aggregated batch requests with shared KV cache? (Action: Eng infra to investigate and report by 2026-12-15)
- Should fallback reasons be enumerated (user-friendly) or retained as internal codes with a human-readable mapping? (Action: Product + Legal to propose framing)
- Are there any security/compliance implications for sharing detailed request traces with customers in dedicated/private setups? (Action: Security to triage)

Appendix (short notes):
- Quick sample support snippets to use in replies:
  - "We can add a quick cost estimate for that route — try the new estimator in Console (coming week). Meanwhile, please include a sample request id and peak concurrency sample and we’ll run a post-mortem."
  - "For private deployments, we recommend starting with our Terraform starter pack and joining a Solutions Eng onboarding session — this typically reduces integration time by ~60% in our pilots."

- Raw ticket IDs sampled: CS-17890, CS-17921, CS-17989 (owners: support L2).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Longer-term: consider a Billing sandbox mode that replays production traces against model-variant cost profiles to forecast monthly bill impact under different configurations. Worth exploring in Optimize product lane.

If you have feedback or want different framing, drop notes here — will iterate before finalizing for the Q1 planning packet.
